messages.content:
Posting: Backend Engineer, Shipment Tracking at Harbor & Pine Logistics
Responsibilities:
1. Build and operate Go services behind the shipment-tracking API, backed by PostgreSQL and Kafka.
2. Find and fix latency problems, using load tests and dashboards to show the change.
3. Design event-driven pipelines that keep tracking data consistent across services.
4. Carry the pager for the services you own and improve their alerts and runbooks.

Candidate
id: lantern-swe
title: Software Engineer at Lantern Freight Systems
tech: Go, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Redis, gRPC, Terraform, GitHub Actions, Prometheus, Grafana, AWS (ECS, RDS)
tags: backend, go, postgresql, kafka, redis, terraform, ci-cd, observability, latency, event-driven, leadership
bullet 1: Cut p99 latency of the shipment-tracking API from 412 ms to 138 ms by replacing a per-request fan-out of 7 queries with one batched query and adding a Redis read-through cache.
bullet 2: Built an idempotent Kafka consumer for carrier status events that deduplicates by event id and sustained 9,200 events/s on a 6-partition topic in staging load tests.
bullet 3: Moved 14 services from hand-written deploy scripts to one shared Terraform and GitHub Actions pipeline, cutting median deploy time from 38 -> 11 minutes.
bullet 4: Added 23 Prometheus alerts and runbooks for the dispatch service; pages per on-call week fell from 31 to 9 over two quarters.
bullet 5: Led a 4-person effort to replace the nightly billing-export cron job with an event-driven job, removing up to 5 hours of data staleness each day.

Candidate
id: marlow-intern
title: Data Engineering Intern at Marlow Data Works
tech: Python, Airflow, dbt, SQL, Snowflake, Docker
tags: data, python, airflow, dbt, sql, etl, data-quality, performance
bullet 1: Built 12 dbt models and an Airflow DAG that replaced a manual weekly spreadsheet report, saving about 6 analyst-hours a week.
bullet 2: Cut the nightly warehouse load from 74 to 29 minutes by partitioning a 310 GB fact table by date and loading only the changed partitions.
bullet 3: Added 41 data-quality tests (not null, uniqueness, referential integrity) that caught 9 upstream schema changes before they reached dashboards.
bullet 4: Reduced the time from a source-table change to a refreshed dashboard by 40.6%, measured as the median over 8 weeks of scheduled runs.
bullet 5: Ended with 28.3% fewer failed Airflow runs over the same 8 weeks after adding retries with backoff and the data-quality tests.

Candidate
id: tidewell-coop
title: Frontend Developer (Co-op) at Tidewell Health Tech
tech: React, TypeScript, Jest, Cypress, REST, Lighthouse
tags: frontend, react, typescript, performance, testing, ab-testing
bullet 1: Rebuilt the patient-intake form in React and TypeScript; form completion rose from 61% to 74% in a 3-week A/B test over 4,800 sessions.
bullet 2: Cut the intake bundle from 612 KB to 238 KB by code-splitting and replacing a charting library, improving median load time on a throttled 4G profile from 5.1 s to 2.4 s.
bullet 3: Wrote 86 Jest unit tests and 14 Cypress end-to-end tests for the intake flow, raising line coverage of the module from 23% to 81%.

Candidate
id: gridlock
title: Gridlock: a distributed rate limiter in Rust and Redis
tech: Rust, Redis, Lua, Tokio, Docker, GitHub Actions
tags: rust, redis, lua, rate-limiting, distributed-systems, backend, benchmarking, fault-tolerance, ci
bullet 1: Built a rate limiter in Rust that keeps token buckets in Redis and updates them with one Lua script, so a check and its update are a single atomic step.
bullet 2: Handled 41,000 checks/s on one 4-vCPU VM against a single Redis instance, with a p99 of 2.1 ms at 20,000 checks/s.
bullet 3: Kept the admitted rate within 2% of the configured limit across 8 limiter processes sharing one Redis, in a 10-minute test at 500 requests/s.
bullet 4: Added a local fallback that degrades to per-process limits when Redis is unreachable, and checked it by killing Redis 50 times during a load test.
bullet 5: Shipped the limiter as a library and an HTTP sidecar with 76 tests and a CI pipeline that runs them against Redis 7.2 and 7.4.

Candidate
id: gridlock-bench
title: Gridlock benchmark harness
tech: Rust, Redis, Make, gnuplot
tags: benchmarking, rust, redis, latency, reproducibility
bullet 1: Wrote a benchmark harness in Rust that sweeps request rates from 1,000 to 50,000 checks/s and records p50, p99 and p99.9 latency at each rate.
bullet 2: Showed that throughput levels off near 41,000 checks/s as the single Redis thread saturates: Redis used 38% of a core at 20,000 checks/s and 99% at 41,000.
bullet 3: Published the raw CSVs and plotting scripts so that every number in the README can be regenerated with one make target.

Candidate
id: raftlet
title: Raftlet: a teaching Raft implementation with a deterministic simulator
tech: Rust, Tokio, Protocol Buffers, proptest
tags: rust, raft, consensus, distributed-systems, simulation, property-testing, fault-tolerance
bullet 1: Implemented leader election, log replication and snapshots from the Raft paper in Rust, with a deterministic simulator that controls the clock, the network and crashes.
bullet 2: Ran 10,000 randomized simulator seeds covering leader crashes, partitions and message loss with 0 safety violations across 5 invariants checked after every step.
bullet 3: Found 3 bugs with the simulator, including a stale-term vote that let a deposed leader commit an entry, and kept each failing seed as a regression test.
bullet 4: Recovered a 5-node cluster to a new leader in a median of 312 simulated ms across 200 simulated leader crashes.

Candidate
id: transit-lake
title: Transit Lake: a batch pipeline over public transit feeds
tech: Python, DuckDB, dbt, Parquet, Airflow, GitHub Actions
tags: data, python, duckdb, dbt, parquet, airflow, etl, data-quality, geospatial
bullet 1: Built a batch pipeline that ingests 48 million GTFS-realtime vehicle positions a month into partitioned Parquet files and models them with dbt on DuckDB.
bullet 2: Loaded one month of data in 6 minutes on a laptop by partitioning by service date and skipping unchanged partitions, down from 41 minutes for a full rebuild.
bullet 3: Added 37 dbt tests and a freshness check that fails the Airflow run when more than 2% of positions are missing a trip id.
bullet 4: Published a reproducible sample of 2 million rows and a make target that rebuilds every table and chart in under 10 minutes.

Candidate
id: tidekv
title: Tidekv: an embedded key-value store in Go
tech: Go, Make, pprof, GitHub Actions
tags: go, storage, lsm, databases, benchmarking, recovery, fault-tolerance, replication
bullet 1: Built an embedded key-value store in Go with a write-ahead log, an in-memory memtable and sorted tables on disk, and recovered the memtable from a log of 8,000 records in 120 ms.
bullet 2: Raised single-threaded write throughput from 7,200 to 18,000 writes/s by enlarging the write buffer from 4 MB to 64 MB, which cut flushes from 910 to 140.
bullet 3: Cut the compaction of a 6 GB data set from 91 s to 29.5 s, a 3.08x speed-up, by merging 4 tables at a time instead of 2.
bullet 4: Lost no acknowledged write across 200 seeded crash-injection runs, each checked against an in-memory model after recovery.
bullet 5: Added a read-only follower that tails the write-ahead log; 2,000 randomized reads returned the same values on the follower and the leader.

Candidate
id: ticket-triage
title: Ticket Triage: a support-ticket classifier
tech: Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, ONNX Runtime, FastAPI, Docker
tags: ml, nlp, pytorch, transformers, onnx, fastapi, classification, evaluation
bullet 1: Fine-tuned a distilled transformer on 38,000 public support tickets to route them into 12 categories, reaching macro-F1 0.87 on a 4,000-ticket held-out set against 0.71 for a TF-IDF and logistic-regression baseline.
bullet 2: Cut CPU inference latency from 41 ms to 9 ms per ticket by exporting to ONNX Runtime and batching, measured on a 4-core laptop.
bullet 3: Served the model with FastAPI in a 310 MB Docker image and added a confidence threshold that sends the 18% of held-out tickets scoring below 0.6 to a human queue.
bullet 4: Wrote an evaluation report with a per-class confusion matrix that showed 3 categories below 0.75 F1 and led to relabelling 420 ambiguous tickets.

Candidate
id: dispatch-desk
title: Dispatch Desk: a tool-using claim-triage agent
tech: Python, Ollama, SQLite, pytest, Docker
tags: python, llm, agents, tool-use, evaluation, testing, ollama
bullet 1: Built a tool-using agent in Python that triages freight-damage claims with an 8B open-weights model served locally by Ollama and one retrieval tool over a SQLite table of 3,200 past claims.
bullet 2: Passed 35 of 40 hand-written claim scenarios (0.875), against 22 of 40 (0.55) for the same model without the retrieval tool.
bullet 3: Recorded every model call and tool call in a SQLite trace, so that a failing scenario replays offline in under 2 s.
bullet 4: Wrote 58 pytest cases, 6 of them replaying recorded traces, and ran them in CI in 4 minutes.

Candidate
id: pulse-dashboard
title: Pulse: a service-health dashboard in React and TypeScript
tech: React, TypeScript, D3, WebSocket, Vite, Vitest, Playwright
tags: frontend, react, typescript, d3, websocket, accessibility, performance, testing
bullet 1: Built a service-health dashboard in React and TypeScript that streams updates over WebSocket and redraws charts of 1,200 points at 58 fps or better in Chrome on a 2021 laptop.
bullet 2: Moved chart rendering from SVG to canvas, cutting the time to draw a 24-hour view from 340 ms to 45 ms.
bullet 3: Added keyboard navigation and ARIA labels; Lighthouse scored accessibility 96 and axe reported 0 violations on the 5 main views.
bullet 4: Covered the main flows with 42 Vitest tests and 9 Playwright end-to-end tests that run in CI in 3.5 minutes.

scores.reason: Candidates directly addressed all responsibilities with Go, Kafka, PostgreSQL, and latency optimization.
Experienced in Python/data engineering tools, not backend Go/Kafka.
Frontend-focused with React/TypeScript, no backend tech mentioned.
Uses Rust/Redis, lacks Go expertise required for API backend.
Python-centric with ML tools, no Go/Kafka/backend experience.
Python and lightweight tools, lacks Go/Kafka backend stack.
Frontend development with React, no backend/backend tools expertise.
